span: DORA's software delivery performance metrics - Throughput
claim: DORA four key metrics are: (1) Deployment frequency, (2) Lead time for changes, (3) Change failure rate, (4) Failed deployment recovery time (MTTR)

span: DORA Continuous Integration - How to implement CI
claim: DORA research shows teams perform better when developers merge their work into trunk at least daily; CI is a core capability driving higher deployment frequency, more stable systems, and higher quality software

Continuous Integration is a software development practice where each member of a team merges their changes into a codebase together with their colleagues' changes at least daily, with each integration verified by an automated build (including test)

Trunk-Based Development focuses on doing all work on Mainline (trunk), avoiding any kind of long-lived branches. Smaller teams commit directly; larger teams use short-lived feature branches (<=2 days)

Trunk-based development is a source-control branching model where developers collaborate in a single branch called trunk and resist pressure to create other long-lived development branches by employing documented techniques

Release Toggles allow incomplete and un-tested codepaths to be shipped to production as latent code; they allow in-progress features to be checked into a shared integration branch while still allowing that branch to be deployed to production at any time; this implements the CD principle of separating release from deployment

The Test Pyramid groups software tests into buckets of different granularity; it gives an idea of how many tests should exist in each group. Composition: many unit tests, fewer integration tests, fewer contract tests, few end-to-end tests

Canary release is a technique to reduce the risk of introducing a new software version in production by slowly rolling out the change to a small subset of users before rolling it out to the entire infrastructure

Blue-green deployment is a release technique that reduces risk and minimizes downtime by running two identical production environments; one serves production, the other is staged; traffic is switched over

SRE is what happens when you ask a software engineer to design an operations team. SRE teams use software engineering approaches to solve operations problems including automation, error budgets, SLOs, and toil reduction

span: SRE Workbook - SLOs, Alerting, On-Call, Postmortem Culture, Canarying Releases
claim: SRE practice includes: implementing SLOs, eliminating toil, on-call practices, incident response, postmortem culture, canarying releases, configuration design and specifics

NIST SSDF v1.1 organizes secure software development practices into four groups: Prepare the Organization (PO), Protect the Software (PS), Produce Well-Secured Software (PW), Respond to Vulnerabilities (RV)
SLSA is a security framework, a checklist of standards and controls to prevent tampering, improve integrity, and secure packages and infrastructure across the software supply chain
OWASP SAMM v2 defines five business functions and fifteen security practices to help organizations assess and improve their software security posture
Observability is the ability to understand the internal state of a system by examining its outputs. In software this is achieved by analyzing telemetry data: traces, metrics, and logs

OpenTelemetry is an observability framework and toolkit designed to facilitate generation, export, and collection of telemetry data (traces, metrics, logs). It is open source, vendor- and tool-agnostic

id.claim: Team Topologies identifies stream-aligned, enabling, complicated-subsystem, and platform team types; the book establishes platform engineering as a first-class organizational pattern and is positioned as the foundation for ROI from AI

claim: Netflix launched its platform engineering initiative in 2017; Airbnb built its own platform on top of Kubernetes around 2019; Thoughtworks Technology Radar 2017 first established the need for platform product management
Google has many generalized engineering practices that cover all languages and all projects; these documents represent their collective experience of best practices
Accelerate presents research linking technical practices (CI, CD, trunk-based development, test automation, monitoring) to organizational performance (profitability, productivity, market share)
Shape Up provides a product development methodology based on shaping work, betting cycles, six-week building cycles, and cooling periods
Team Topologies identifies four team types: stream-aligned, enabling, complicated-subsystem, and platform teams. The book establishes platform engineering as a first-class organizational pattern
GitHub/Accenture study found developers using GitHub Copilot completed coding tasks 55% faster than the control group, with high satisfaction

GitHub Copilot works best for: writing tests and repetitive code, debugging syntax, explaining code, generating regular expressions. Copilot is not designed to: respond to non-coding prompts, replace developer expertise

Anthropic defines workflows (predetermined tool sequences including prompt chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestrator-workers, evaluator-optimizer) and agents (LLMs using tools based on environmental feedback in a loop). Agents begin work with a command from or discussion with a human; once the task is clear, they plan and operate independently

Anthropic's Claude Code is an agentic coding environment. It reads files, runs commands, makes changes, and autonomously works through problems. Best practices are based on the constraint that Claude's context window fills up fast. Key practices: explore-plan-implement loop, test-driven development, context management, allow-list tooling
OpenAI Codex is a cloud-based software engineering agent that can work on many tasks in parallel, powered by codex-1
SWE-bench is the industry-standard benchmark for AI coding agents evaluated on real GitHub issues. SWE-bench Verified is the human-validated subset
In 2024 Python overtook JavaScript as the most-used language on GitHub; AI is a major driver. AI is expanding the global developer community
Chaos Engineering is the discipline of experimenting on a distributed system to build confidence in the system's capability to withstand turbulent conditions in production
Stripe's API versioning philosophy prioritizes additive changes, deprecation grace periods, and design for stability. Versioned at the API surface; not at deployment
GitLab is remote-first, async-first; uses merge requests for code review; uses single deploy button via ChatOps; follows a documented engineering process
GitLab security practices include threat modeling, secure code review, dependency scanning, container scanning, dynamic analysis, and a security assurance team
Google's framework pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization
Microsoft's framework pillars: cost optimization, operational excellence, performance efficiency, reliability, security
AWS's framework pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, sustainability (added later)
Bazel is a build system designed for large monorepos, providing hermetic, reproducible builds with remote caching and parallel execution
2025 DORA report focuses on unlocking the value of AI by investing in teams and people, not just tooling
81.4% of developers used OpenAI GPT models in past year; 42.8% used Claude Sonnet; 35.3% used Gemini Flash for development work. AI Agents section tracks agentic workflows
NIST SP 800-218A is the SSDF Community Profile for Generative AI and Dual-Use Foundation Models, augmenting SP 800-218 with practices specific to AI model development throughout the SDLC
CNCF TAG App Delivery is the technical advisory group for application delivery; defines the scope of platform engineering, CI/CD, GitOps, and progressive delivery
Backstage is an open source IDP framework originally built at Spotify, now a CNCF project; provides service catalog, scaffolding, golden paths, and developer portal
CNCF hosts graduated and incubating projects including Kubernetes, Argo, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Backstage, etcd, and many more
Microservices and other modern architectures should be designed for evolution: support incremental change in architecture, use fitness functions, and avoid big-bang rewrites
Strangler Fig is a pattern for incrementally migrating legacy systems by growing a new system alongside the old, gradually replacing functionality

span: How to break a Monolith into Microservices
claim: Decomposing a monolith into microservices requires identifying seams, prioritizing by business value, using the strangler fig pattern, and accepting it is a long process

Microservice Architecture is a particular way of designing software applications as suites of independently deployable services. Characteristics: componentization via services, organized around business capability, decentralized governance, decentralized data management, infrastructure automation, smart endpoints and dumb pipes
CI/CD pipelines orchestrate automated builds, tests, and deployments as a single release workflow

Lock-in is not a simple true-or-false matter; managed services offer productivity gains that should be weighed against the lock-in cost; architectural energy spent on lock-in reduction should be proportional to actual risk
Data Mesh: federated data ownership, data as a product, self-serve data platform, and federated computational governance
Distributed systems patterns catalog including consensus, replication, partitioning, eventual consistency, and other recurring solutions
